predecessors.name: Seleucid Empire
predecessors.text: the land between the Upper and Lower Zab with Arbela as capital, 'eventually' with Nineveh, the Zagros on the east

successors.name: Sasanian Empire
successors.text: the kingdom 'transformed into a province (shahr)' c.

ledger.x: c. 164 BC: a kingdom of Adiabene appears at Arbela. 'coinage implies the establishment of a kingdom in Adiabene around 164 BCE', after the collapse of Seleucid rule; Mithridates I conquered it 'between 145 and 141 BCE' and it was a Parthian vassal from then.
145-141 BC: Adiabene becomes a Parthian vassal.
88-85 BC: Tigranes the Great takes Adiabene from Parthia.
88-85 BC: Adiabene becomes an Armenian vassal.
66 BC (bridged): Armenian overlordship ends.
66 BC (bridged): Adiabene is a Parthian vassal again.
Late 1st century BC: Gordyene becomes an Adiabenian dependency.
36: Artabanus II gives Nisibis to Izates II.
116: Trajan makes Adiabene part of the Roman province of Assyria.
116: Gordyene's dependency on Adiabene ends with Adiabene's annexation.

116: the Parthian vassalage is interrupted by Trajan's annexation ('The region was later made a part of the Roman province of Assyria after the invasion by Trajan in 116'); the 116 loss event carries the land.
117: Hadrian gives Adiabene back.
117: Adiabene is a Parthian vassal again.
165: Nisibis falls to Rome.
224: the Parthian overlordship ends.
224: Adiabene a Sasanian vassal.
299: Rome takes the Tigris-to-Greater-Zab part of Adiabene.
363: the Roman part of Adiabene is lost again, so the Sasanian vassal kingdom has its full core back.

c. 379: the Sasanian vassalage ends with the kingdom itself ('Vassal of the Sasanian Empire (224-379)'; 'transformed into a province (shahr), governed by a non-royal delegate'); the dissolve event follows.

c. 379: the kingdom becomes a Sasanian province. After Ardashir II the kingdom 'was after his tenure in c. 379 transformed into a province (shahr)' governed by a non-royal delegate; it stayed Sasanian 'until the Muslim conquest of Persia'.

wars.name: Trajan's Parthian campaign
wars.outcome: Adiabene was invaded in 116 and made part of the Roman province of Assyria; Hadrian restored it in 117.

wars.name: Roman-Parthian War of 161-166
wars.outcome: Roman victory with minor gains in upper Mesopotamia; Nisibis besieged and captured in 165.

wars.name: Roman-Parthian war of Septimius Severus
wars.outcome: 'in 196 three divisions of the Roman army fell upon Adiabene'; no land is recorded as changing hands there.

wars.name: Roman-Parthian war of Caracalla
wars.outcome: 'Caracalla took Arbela in the year 216' and destroyed the royal tombs; no occupation is recorded.

wars.name: Fall of the Parthian Empire to Ardashir I
wars.outcome: 'The Parthians were overthrown by the Sasanian Empire in 224'; Adiabene's feudatory dynasties resisted Sasanian advances until Sasanian rule was established 'by the time of Shapur I (r.

certainty.note: The page gives only the Zab rivers, the Zagros and Nineveh as bounds, and its own sources disagree on whether Nisibis was inside; no treaty line.
